column1: # The fetch menu: what a fetch can read, for `ngsdose fetchplan`.
# A fetch (`ngs-dose count -m fetch`) reads the control regions and the sink intervals of the classes
# it loads, through the CRAM index. Sinks are where the aligner put a class's reads; they are learned
# from whole-file scans (`ngsdose sinks SCANS [--classes ...]`) and checked on held-out scans
# (`ngsdose sinks HELD_OUT --evaluate BED`), never assumed from the class's reference coordinates, and
# they belong to one aligner and reference. A new class starts as a candidate: its panel is loaded in
# the scans (fetchplan writes it to PREFIX.scan_panels.txt), its sinks are learned there, and only
# then does its row name a sinks file and become fetchable.
# Format: tab-separated. Lines starting with '#' are comments, except '##preset<TAB>name<TAB>description',
# which describes a preset. The first other line is the header; columns may come in any order, and
#   class     option name: the class name as its panel defines it (checked against the panel's ##class
#             lines), 'controls' / 'unmapped' for the two special rows, or the name of a subset
#   kind      positional | compositional (as in the panel) | controls | unmapped | subset: a named subset of a
#             class's learned intervals (one array of a satellite family), whose sinks file is a BED of those
#             intervals with the class in its fourth column (experimental/subsets/NAME.bed). It is fetched
#             whole and counted as that class, and `ngsdose estimate` reports NAME.mass_Mb from the class's
#             placements inside it; fetched without the rest of the class's sinks, the class itself is not
#   status    shipped | experimental | candidate, optionally followed by ': a note'.
#             shipped: sinks in the bundle (fetch compared with scans for rDNA45S, rDNA5S and DJ; not yet
#             for TEL); experimental: sinks learned from scans, not yet shipped or compared; candidate: no
#   tier      A-D, the order in which `--budget-mb` adds options (cheapest first within a tier):
#             A core (always worth its bytes), B shipped and measured, C experimental with a named
#             question and truth data, D experimental, costly or of lower capture
#   presets   comma-separated preset names the row belongs to ('-' for none)
#   panel     the k-mer panel file defining the class (for a subset: its class), relative to this file's
#   sinks     the sinks BED holding the class's intervals (4th column = class), relative to this file's
#             directory; for the controls row, the BED of the control regions; '-' for unmapped and candidates
#   truth     external truth available for the 1000 Genomes samples ('-' if none)
#   stats     optional column: interval statistics (`ngsdose sinks SCANS --evaluate BED --held-out --stats FILE`,
#             on scans the sinks were not learned from, which the file's '# held-out:' line records) for
#             `fetchplan --capture`, relative to this file's directory ('-' for none, and for subsets; a named
#             file that is missing is skipped); `fetchplan --stats` adds or overrides them. A capture target keeps
#             a class's intervals by share per read, or with --crai by share per byte of their own fetch (the CRAM
#             slices they overlap, with their containers' compression headers; then the expected capture is a
#             lower bound, from the statistics' share_max). An interval another selected class keeps is read
#             anyway: every class that has it keeps it
# The control regions are always read: the set the controls row names, or another of the bundle's control sets
# (`fetchplan --controls NAME`; `ngsdose control-sets` lists them: `all`, every region the bundle has, which is what a
# whole-file scan counts; `base`; `lite200`; `karyotype` and `screen`, which add the karyotype windows to lite200's
# controls). The unmapped bin is every read without a coordinate
# (`ngs-dose count --unmapped`). Costs are per CRAM and come from its .crai (`fetchplan --crai`), priced as
# `ngs-dose count -m fetch` reads them: one query per run of intervals no more than 50,000 bp apart (an engine before
# 0.3.0: per run of touching or overlapping intervals), each decoding every slice that overlaps it, so a slice under
# several queries is decoded once per query. The MB figures
# below are medians over 13 NYGC 30x CRAM indexes (docs/fetch_examples.md, which prices every option and the
# presets and is the figure to re-run).
